exposure: Early induction of labour (within 12 hours of premature rupture of membranes)
Late induction of labour (after 12 hours of premature rupture of membranes)
cohort: 164 pregnant women aged 18-35 years, with uncomplicated pregnancies at 37-40 weeks gestational age, premature rupture of membranes, reactive CTG, adequate pelvis, clear liquor, and vertex presentation.
finding: For women with term premature rupture of membranes, earlier induction of labour results in lower maternal morbidity (less chorioamnionitis and post-partum haemorrhage) and lower fetal morbidity (less neonatal sepsis and poor APGAR scores).
mod_finding: 21% of women had instrumental vaginal delivery and 19% had caesarian section in the overall cohort.
